positioning.text: Kaiser Permanente says it exists to provide high-quality, affordable health care services and to improve the health of its members and communities, with care focused on members' total health and a model that integrates care and coverage.
positioning.quote: Care for members and patients focuses on their total health.

evidence.title: Our Mission | Kaiser Permanente
evidence.quote: Care for members and patients focuses on their total health.

evidence.title: Health Care That Works | Kaiser Permanente
evidence.quote: Kaiser Permanente's unique model integrates care and coverage at every stage of life.

facts.text: Kaiser Permanente's Fast Facts page lists 12.8M members nationally, with data as of September 30, 2026, across regions that include Georgia (446,948 members) and the Mid-Atlantic States (736,189 members; Baltimore, Washington, D.C., Northern Virginia and Suburban Maryland).

evidence.title: Fast Facts | Kaiser Permanente
evidence.quote: Data as of September 30, 2026, unless otherwise noted.

facts.text: The Thrive advertising campaign began in 2004; a 2014 Kaiser Permanente release called it the organization's longest-running campaign and listed TV, radio, print, online and out-of-home ads.

evidence.title: A Decade After its Launch, Kaiser Permanente's Thrive Campaign Highlights Ease and Accessibility of High-Quality Care in Age of Digital Health
evidence.quote: The 2014 Thrive launch marks the 11th year of the campaign.

facts.text: In March 2023 Becker's reported that Kaiser Permanente had refreshed its brand promise with its first new campaign in about 20 years, led by national chief marketing officer Kristy LoRusso.

evidence.title: 'It all comes back to storytelling': How Kaiser's marketing chief brings the brand to life
evidence.quote: Ms. LoRusso is excited about Kaiser's refreshed "brand promise," its first new campaign in about 20 years

facts.text: The brand campaign "A Better Idea for Health Care", created by Droga5 and launched in select markets in 2025, went national in June 2026 with ads featuring soccer player Son Heung-min across digital, social, audio, film and out-of-home channels.

evidence.title: Kaiser Permanente taps soccer star for nationwide brand campaign
evidence.quote: The campaign, which launched in select markets in 2025, will roll out across digital, social, audio, film and out-of-home channels.

evidence.title: Kaiser Permanente is a better idea for health care
evidence.quote: the debut of the new films starring Son usher in the campaign's expansion to the national stage.

facts.text: Find Your Words was announced by Kaiser Permanente Colorado on May 1, 2017 as a public health awareness campaign on depression using TV, radio and online messages; on 2026-11-10 findyourwords.org redirected to a kp.org page presenting it as a mental health resource for young people.

evidence.title: Kaiser Permanente Launches "Find Your Words" Campaign to Fight Stigma Around Mental Health

strengths.text: Brand platforms run for a long time: Thrive began in 2004, and trade coverage in 2023 and in 2026 each described the newer work as the first of its kind in 20 or more years.
The current campaign advertises the coordinated care model itself, so the brand message and the organization's stated differentiator are the same thing.
Mental health is covered at three levels: a public awareness resource, a care section on the member site, and consumer apps offered to members.
Utility content and tools (health encyclopedia, recipes, app) give members reasons to return to owned properties outside of an ad flight.

gaps.text: As of 2026-11-10 the Thrive name survives in two social handles while the Thrive web address redirects and the current brand platform carries a different name.
The newest KP Research Radio episode shown on its page on 2026-11-10 was dated January 9, 2025.

opportunitiesForUpmc.text: Kaiser Permanente lists members in the Mid-Atlantic States and Georgia, so its brand work is a relevant benchmark for East Coast markets and should not be treated as West Coast only.
Test how clearly UPMC's own advertising explains coordination between care and coverage, which is the idea the current Kaiser Permanente campaign leads with.
Compare UPMC's mental health content against the three-level pattern here: a public awareness resource, a care section, and member apps.
Review whether UPMC's app has a public, plain-language feature page comparable to the Kaiser Permanente app page.
